ColdChain Quality Manual v4.2
Quality Assurance – Perth Distribution Facility
Document ID: QM-PER-042
Revision: 4.2
Review Date: 14 July 2026
Next Scheduled Review: January 2027
Owner: Quality Assurance Manager
Applies to: All cold storage operations, including Zones A, B, C, and D

---

1. Purpose and Scope

1.1 This manual defines the minimum quality and temperature control requirements for all cold storage and handling activities conducted at the Perth facility. It applies to all permanent staff, casual workers, contractors, and third-party logistics providers operating within the facility.

1.2 The requirements herein are aligned with APAC Good Distribution Practice guidelines and relevant Australian cold chain standards. Where local conditions require stricter control, the stricter requirement applies.

1.3 This revision supersedes all previous versions. Any printed copy of this manual is considered uncontrolled unless accompanied by a stamp from the Quality Assurance office.

---

2. Temperature Setpoints and Classification

2.1 The facility operates four primary cold storage zones. Each zone has a designated setpoint that must be maintained continuously. Setpoints are established based on product requirements and validated through annual mapping studies.

2.2 Zone designations and setpoints:

| Zone | Setpoint (°C) | Acceptance Range (°C) | Primary Product Types |
|------|---------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Zone A | -18.0 | -20.0 to -16.0 | Frozen meat, seafood, prepared meals |
| Zone B | -25.0 | -27.0 to -23.0 | Ice cream, frozen desserts, sensitive proteins |
| Zone C | 2.0 | 0.5 to 4.0 | Fresh produce, dairy, chilled beverages |
| Zone D | 5.0 | 3.0 to 7.0 | Pharmaceuticals requiring chilled storage |

2.3 Zone A has_temperature_setpoint -18.0 celsius. Record status: current. This setpoint is current and controlled as of this revision. No change to the Zone A setpoint is pending or under evaluation at the time of publication.

2.4 Any proposed change to a zone setpoint must be submitted as a change control request through the Quality Assurance department. Proposed changes are reviewed against product safety requirements, customer specifications, and regulatory obligations before approval.

2.5 Temporary excursions beyond the acceptance range must be handled per Section 6 (Corrective Actions) and must not be normalised or accepted without documented investigation.

---

3. Cold Chain Compliance Requirements

3.1 All staff handling temperature-sensitive product must complete cold chain awareness training annually. Training records are maintained by the Human Resources department and audited during internal quality reviews.

3.2 Temperature monitoring devices must be calibrated at intervals not exceeding six months. Calibration certificates must be retained for a minimum of three years and made available upon request.

3.3 Each zone must have a minimum of two independent temperature sensors. One sensor is designated as the primary monitoring point, the other as a backup. The backup sensor must be within the same zone and positioned to provide meaningful redundancy.

3.4 Temperature readings must be recorded at least every 10 minutes. Recording intervals may be reduced during periods of high activity or when doors are opened frequently, but must never be increased beyond 10 minutes.

3.5 Daily temperature logs must be reviewed by the shift supervisor and signed off. Any anomaly noted during review must be escalated to the Quality Assurance team within one business day.

3.6 Product received from external suppliers must be checked for temperature compliance at the point of receipt. Receiving staff must verify that the product temperature is within the acceptance range for the intended storage zone before unloading.
4.6 Alarm delays are intended to prevent nuisance alarms caused by brief door openings or evaporator defrost cycles. The delay commences once the temperature has crossed the alarm threshold. If the temperature remains beyond the threshold at the end of the delay period, the alarm is activated.

4.7 All alarms are logged by the monitoring system with a timestamp, zone identifier, sensor identifier, and the temperature at the time of alarm. The system must also record when the alarm was acknowledged and when the condition was resolved.

4.8 Alarm acknowledgement procedure:

a) The shift supervisor, or a trained delegate, must acknowledge all alarms within thirty (30) minutes of activation;
b) Acknowledging an alarm does not clear it. The alarm remains active until the temperature returns within the acceptable range;
c) The person acknowledging the alarm must record their name, the time of acknowledgement, and any immediate actions taken;
d) If the alarm condition persists for more than sixty (60) minutes, the Quality Assurance team must be notified.

4.9 In the event of a power failure, the monitoring system must operate on battery backup for a minimum of four (4) hours. The battery backup must be tested monthly and the test result recorded in the maintenance log.

4.10 All temperature monitoring equipment must be connected to an uninterruptible power supply where installed. Portable temperature loggers used during transport or temporary storage must be charged and verified before each use.

5. Documentation and Record Keeping

5.1 Temperature records must be retained for a minimum of three (3) years from the date of recording. Records must be legible, traceable to the zone and sensor they relate to, and protected from unauthorised alteration.

Zone B has_temperature_setpoint -22.0 celsius. Record status: current.

5.2 The following records must be maintained and made available for inspection:

a) Continuous temperature logs for each zone;
b) Daily temperature review sheets, signed by the shift supervisor;
c) Calibration certificates for all temperature monitoring equipment;
d) Alarm logs, including acknowledgement and resolution details;
e) Corrective action reports relating to temperature excursions;
f) Training records for cold chain awareness;
g) Maintenance records for monitoring systems and refrigeration plant.

5.3 Daily temperature review sheets must include the following information:

a) Date and shift;
b) Zone identifier(s);
c) Minimum and maximum temperature recorded during the shift;
d) Any alarms activated, with times and actions taken;
e) Any door opening events exceeding fifteen (15) minutes;
f) Signature of the shift supervisor undertaking the review.

5.4 Completed daily review sheets must be submitted to the Quality Assurance department no later than the end of the following business day. Sheets may be submitted electronically via the shared quality drive, or in hard copy where electronic submission is not available.

5.5 Any temperature excursion, defined as a recorded temperature outside the acceptable range for the zone for more than fifteen (15) minutes, must be documented using the Temperature Excursion Report form (Form QF-17). The form must be completed by the shift supervisor and submitted to Quality Assurance within one (1) business day of the excursion being identified.

5.6 The Temperature Excursion Report must include:

a) Date and time of the excursion;
b) Zone and sensor identifier;
c) Duration of the excursion;
d) Recorded minimum or maximum temperature;
e) Suspected cause;
f) Product affected, including product type, quantity, and batch numbers where known;
g) Disposition of affected product;
h) Preventative actions taken to avoid recurrence.
6. EQUIPMENT MAINTENANCE

6.1 General Requirements

All refrigeration plant and temperature monitoring equipment shall be maintained in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and the maintenance schedules detailed in Appendix B of this manual. Maintenance activities shall be recorded on the appropriate maintenance log sheets and retained for a minimum of three (3) years.

6.2 Preventive Maintenance Schedule

a) Refrigeration compressors and condensers: monthly inspection and cleaning as required;
b) Evaporator coils and fans: quarterly inspection, cleaning, and condensate drain check;
c) Door seals and strip curtains: weekly visual inspection, replacement when worn or damaged;
d) Temperature sensors and data loggers: six (6) monthly calibration verification against a certified reference thermometer;
e) Backup generator: monthly run test under load for a minimum of thirty (30) minutes;
f) Emergency alarm system: quarterly functional test, including audible and visual indicators.

6.3 Breakdown Maintenance

Where a breakdown occurs, the following procedure shall be followed:

a) The shift supervisor shall be notified immediately;
b) Product shall be assessed for risk and, where necessary, transferred to alternate storage in accordance with Section 4.6;
c) The maintenance contractor shall be contacted in accordance with the service agreement;
d) A Maintenance Breakdown Report (Form QF-21) shall be completed and submitted to Quality Assurance within one (1) business day;
e) The incident shall be reviewed at the next scheduled quality meeting to identify any systemic issues.

6.4 Calibration

Calibration of all temperature monitoring equipment shall be performed by an accredited calibration service provider. Calibration certificates shall be reviewed by the Quality Assurance department to confirm that equipment is operating within acceptable tolerances. Equipment failing calibration shall be removed from service immediately and replaced or repaired before further use. A register of all monitoring equipment, including calibration due dates, shall be maintained by the Quality Assurance department and reviewed monthly.

7. TRAINING

7.1 Induction Training

All new employees shall complete cold chain induction training prior to commencing work in any temperature-controlled area. Induction training shall cover:

a) The importance of maintaining temperature integrity;
b) Correct handling procedures for temperature-sensitive product;
c) Operation of temperature monitoring equipment;
d) Alarm response procedures;
e) Emergency procedures, including product transfer and isolation.

7.2 Refresher Training

Refresher training shall be undertaken by all staff at least annually. Refresher training shall include any changes to procedures, review of recent excursions or incidents, and reinforcement of good cold chain practices. Training records shall be maintained in each employee's personnel file and a summary register shall be held by the Quality Assurance department.

7.3 Training Records

Training records shall include:

a) Employee name and position;
b) Date and type of training completed;
c) Name of trainer or training provider;
d) Assessment outcome, where applicable;
e) Date of next required refresher.

7.4 Competency Assessment

Where a role involves specific cold chain responsibilities, competency shall be assessed at the time of induction and annually thereafter. Assessment methods may include written tests, practical demonstrations, or observed performance. Staff who do not demonstrate competency shall receive additional training and be reassessed within fourteen (14) days.

8. INTERNAL AUDIT

8.1 Audit Schedule

Internal audits of the cold chain management system shall be conducted at least twice per calendar year. The audit schedule shall be prepared by the Quality Assurance department and approved by the General Manager. Audits shall cover all zones and all applicable procedures. Additional audits may be conducted where significant changes to processes, equipment, or personnel have occurred, or where a serious excursion or customer complaint has been identified.

documents.title: ColdChain Ops Chat – 14–17 Jul 2026
documents.content:
07:42 Sofia
morning. i had a look at the pallets that came in over night from the rail. half the cartons on the 3 pallets for the north route have damp spots. not leaking but looks like condensation. flagging before i put them in the chiller.

07:44 Priya
Thanks Sofia. Can you take a photo and log them as suspect? I'll come down and we can decide if they need quarantine. Condensation on the outer carton isn't always a reject, but I want to check the internal temp probe on at least one.

07:46 Sofia
will do. photos up in the portal now. probe reading on the one i checked was 2.1°C which is fine for the chiller but not for the freezer line, so im guessing they were on the dock a while

07:50 Tom
Sofia if the probe said 2.1 they def sat out. freezer line should be -18 to -22. that rail yard has no shade and it was 32 yesterday arvo. I'd quarantine the whole lot if it was me.

07:52 Priya
Let's not jump ahead. I'll inspect at 9:30. Marcus, can we hold the north route load until I give the go?

07:53 Marcus
Yeah hold it. Dave tell dispatch the 11am north pickup is delayed pending QA. Send update to the client pls.

07:55 Dave
done. sent them the standard "minor inspection delay" msg. they asked for ETA, I said by 12.

08:30 Lena
morning all. just did the 8am walk through. ambient temp in the main hall is 16.2, chiller 2 is running a bit warm at 3.4 but within range. freezer 1 and 2 both steady at -21. HVAC filter alarm went off at 7:58, not critical but will need replacing this week.

08:32 Tom
Lena can you log the filter alarm in the maintenance tracker? I'll grab a filter from stores tomorrow. the dock light is done btw, replaced ballast and it's working. also checked the door seals on bay 4, theyre fine.

08:34 Lena
logged. also the weather says 35 today, so if anyone is loading after 2pm take water breaks. i have extra bottles in the break room.

09:30 Priya
Sofia and I inspected the suspect pallets. Condensation is only on the outer layer, internal temps all good (range 1.8–2.4). No sign of freeze damage. I'm releasing them for the chiller, but they should not go to the freezer line. I've marked the pallet tags with a yellow stripe so they don't get mixed up.

09:32 Marcus
Good. Dave, release the north route. Sofia, put those pallets in chiller 3, not chiller 2, so we keep them separate from the main stock.

ColdChain Logistics Pty Ltd has_primary_site Perth Cold Storage Facility. Record status: current.

09:34 Sofia
got it, moving them now. chiller 3 is empty anyway.

10:00 Tom
Temp check done. all probes reading normal. chiller 2 still at 3.4 but that's within the 2–4 band so no action needed. freezer defrost cycle ran at 9:45 as scheduled, no issues.

10:15 Dave
Client confirmed they're happy with the delay, no penalty. North route truck leaving at 12:15 as planned.

11:20 Sofia
back from lunch. does anyone know if the pallet jack in bay 2 is fixed? i need it for the 1pm pick list.

11:22 Tom
fixed it yesterday arvo. new wheel. it's fine now.

11:23 Sofia
thx. also the radio in the forklift is dead, not a big deal but if anyone knows how to fix it let me know.

11:25 Tom
probably the antenna cable. i'll look at it after my afternoon checks.

13:15 Sofia
north route loaded and gone. all good.

15:40 Lena

ColdChain Quality Manual v4.2
Quality Assurance – Perth Distribution Facility
Document ID: QM-PER-042
Revision: 4.2
Review Date: 14 July 2026
Next Scheduled Review: January 2027
Owner: Quality Assurance Manager
Applies to: All cold storage operations, including Zones A, B, C, and D

---

1. Purpose and Scope

1.1 This manual defines the minimum quality and temperature control requirements for all cold storage and handling activities conducted at the Perth facility. It applies to all permanent staff, casual workers, contractors, and third-party logistics providers operating within the facility.

1.2 The requirements herein are aligned with APAC Good Distribution Practice guidelines and relevant Australian cold chain standards. Where local conditions require stricter control, the stricter requirement applies.

1.3 This revision supersedes all previous versions. Any printed copy of this manual is considered uncontrolled unless accompanied by a stamp from the Quality Assurance office.

---

2. Temperature Setpoints and Classification

2.1 The facility operates four primary cold storage zones. Each zone has a designated setpoint that must be maintained continuously. Setpoints are established based on product requirements and validated through annual mapping studies.

2.2 Zone designations and setpoints:

| Zone | Setpoint (°C) | Acceptance Range (°C) | Primary Product Types |
|------|---------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Zone A | -18.0 | -20.0 to -16.0 | Frozen meat, seafood, prepared meals |
| Zone B | -25.0 | -27.0 to -23.0 | Ice cream, frozen desserts, sensitive proteins |
| Zone C | 2.0 | 0.5 to 4.0 | Fresh produce, dairy, chilled beverages |
| Zone D | 5.0 | 3.0 to 7.0 | Pharmaceuticals requiring chilled storage |

2.3 Zone A has_temperature_setpoint -18.0 celsius. Record status: current. This setpoint is current and controlled as of this revision. No change to the Zone A setpoint is pending or under evaluation at the time of publication.

2.4 Any proposed change to a zone setpoint must be submitted as a change control request through the Quality Assurance department. Proposed changes are reviewed against product safety requirements, customer specifications, and regulatory obligations before approval.

2.5 Temporary excursions beyond the acceptance range must be handled per Section 6 (Corrective Actions) and must not be normalised or accepted without documented investigation.

---

3. Cold Chain Compliance Requirements

3.1 All staff handling temperature-sensitive product must complete cold chain awareness training annually. Training records are maintained by the Human Resources department and audited during internal quality reviews.

3.2 Temperature monitoring devices must be calibrated at intervals not exceeding six months. Calibration certificates must be retained for a minimum of three years and made available upon request.

3.3 Each zone must have a minimum of two independent temperature sensors. One sensor is designated as the primary monitoring point, the other as a backup. The backup sensor must be within the same zone and positioned to provide meaningful redundancy.

3.4 Temperature readings must be recorded at least every 10 minutes. Recording intervals may be reduced during periods of high activity or when doors are opened frequently, but must never be increased beyond 10 minutes.

3.5 Daily temperature logs must be reviewed by the shift supervisor and signed off. Any anomaly noted during review must be escalated to the Quality Assurance team within one business day.

3.6 Product received from external suppliers must be checked for temperature compliance at the point of receipt. Receiving staff must verify that the product temperature is within the acceptance range for the intended storage zone before unloading.
